Date: 2026-12-01T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Atlas Retail POC — alignment + action plan

Thanks for the time today, Elaine and Tom — great conversation and lots of alignment on objectives. Quick recap and proposed action plan so we have a single source of truth going into the POC.

Call highlights (capture of what we agreed)
- Goal: prove end-to-end inference for product search ranking with quantifiable business metrics.
- Success criteria (customer-defined):
  - P95 inference latency <= 300ms on standard sample queries at 1k QPS burst / 50 rps sustained test
  - Relative ranking uplift >= 6% on internal A/B metric compared to baseline model
  - No persistent storage of raw customer queries in our hosted logs (session-only KV cache, 90-day retention for aggregated logs)
  - Audit logs + model version tagging for each call
- What we will deliver in the POC: hosted test endpoint (Redwood hosted), sample evaluation harness (scripts + metrics spreadsheet), network requirements doc for your infra team.

Proposed timeline (two-stage, 3-week view)
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, vendor docs (SOC2 summary, DFIR contacts), procurement questionnaire started
- Week 1: env provision + shared test data ingestion, basic smoke tests (latency/throughput)
- Week 2: run evaluation scripts, iterate on prompt/config, collect metrics and run simple A/B compare
- Week 3: readout + go/no-go (decision meeting)

Ownership (first-pass) — who to loop for each lane
- Integration & app-side orchestration: Marissa Cole (Responsible), Hannah Schmitt (Accountable)
- Redwood infra provisioning (VPC peering, GPU pool): Karthik Iyer (Responsible), Dylan Brooks (Accountable)
- Security & compliance (SOC2 artifacts, data residency): Irene Choi (Responsible), Hannah Schmitt (Accountable)
- Procurement & contracting: Ben Carter (Responsible), Hannah Schmitt (Accountable)

Attachments & links
- Attached: atlas-poc-success-metrics.xlsx (proposal for the evaluation metrics table)
- Attached: network-requirements.pdf (initial ports/IPs and peering notes)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAtlasPOC

Immediate asks for Atlas team
1) Please confirm the success criteria above or edit where needed (latency/throughput targets).
2) Tom — can your infra team review the attached network-requirements.pdf and call out any peering/VPN constraints?
3) Elaine — procurement requested a vendor questionnaire; can you share the contact or drop procurement@atlasretail.com into thread?

Next internal step: I’ll schedule a 30-min internal sync (Redwood-only) to make sure the artifact owners above can ship the first set of deliverables by EOD Monday.

Thanks — looking forward.

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com]

Subject: Re: Atlas Retail POC — alignment + action plan

Thanks, Hannah — concise recap, appreciate it. A couple of notes from our side after the team debrief:

Constraints / asks from Atlas
- Procurement will need a completed vendor questionnaire and SOC 2 summary before we can spin up any hosted endpoints for trial (they already got an introductory packet). Procurement contact is procurement@atlasretail.com (CC'd).
- Security wants a short data flow diagram and clarification that raw search queries will not be persisted to object storage; aggregated logs with 90-day retention is fine.
- Ops: we prefer not to open customer-facing ports directly; ask if Redwood can support either a short-lived VPN or AWS PrivateLink for the POC.

Tom (cc) — can you review the network doc Hannah attached and flag any immediate redlines?

We are aligned on the high-level success metrics; I’ll confirm the A/B metric definition with analytics and come back with a target window for the uplift metric (should be in your metrics sheet).

Happy to move forward — please send the SOC2 summary and a short one-page security note that Irene can expand on.

Best,
Elaine
Director, Data Science & Search
Atlas Retail
